title: Bill Burr Argues for AI to Replace CEOs Instead of Workers
key_facts: Comedian Bill Burr, in a Rolling Stone interview, argued that companies should build AI CEOs rather than AI workers, per the Yahoo article.
Burr asked: why not make an AI CEO that is empathetic and cares about the middle class and the future of the planet.
He said replacing one person at the top saves more money than replacing many workers, and that AI is 'not for us, it's for them'.
The article says the average CEO-to-worker pay ratio at large public companies is near 290 to 1, without naming a source.

The interview also covers his Broadway run in Glengarry Glen Ross and his next film, Aaron Sorkin's The Social Reckoning, built around 2021 Wall Street Journal reporting on the Facebook whistleblower.
quote_evidence: All this AI is to replace working people.
Because it's not for us, it's for them.
The average CEO-to-worker pay ratio at large public companies sits near 290 to 1.
why_it_matters_hint: A well-known comedian is voicing a common worker complaint: AI is aimed at cutting workers' jobs, not bosses' pay.
notes: Yahoo page appears to carry a Complex entertainment piece; the original Rolling Stone interview was not read. Interview date not stated. The 290 to 1 figure is unsourced in the article. The article also discusses other interview topics, left out.
